precepts.text: Whoever will not receive you, shake off the very dust from your feet and wash your hands of them.
precepts.point: Give not that which is holy unto the dogs nor cast your pearls before swine: there is no magic scripture, you cannot save everyone, and some are predestined to be stupid.

note.label: Untruthful Trinity Revisited & Ridiculous

precepts.why:
“Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet, and turn again and rend you.” Don't waste your time talking to dumbass people; they'll turn against you and fight you. There is no magic scripture. You cannot save everyone. Some people are meant, predestined, to be stupid.

Luke gives the instruction Christ gave: “And whosoever will not receive you, when ye go out of that city, shake off the very dust from your feet for a testimony against them.” Shake off the very dust. Wash your hands of them and leave them alone.

If you explain that the heavenly Father is the Most High God, that he has a son, and that his son has sons, the children of Israel, and they can't understand it and say no, they're all one, leave that negro alone. You're wasting your time; he is on medications or should be.

The proverbs read with it say the same: “If a wise man contendeth with a foolish man, whether he rage or laugh, there is no rest.” There is no conclusion; it is a circular argument that goes nowhere. “The heart of the foolish is like a cartwheel; and his thoughts are like a rolling axletree.” Three is one, one is three, round and round. These are unreasonable people, so you shake off the dust and move on.

precepts.text: Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven. And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity. That goes back to what we just read: this guy that was in the truth, he took his talent, hid it in a napkin. I'm not helping them anymore; I did it full time, but I don't want to do it no more.
precepts.point: But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me. Churches don't read that; churches will look at that and go, no, we're not reading that in Sunday school. You know what it means further? You ain't going to just be able to do what you want to do. You was put on this earth to do what the Most High and Christ said, and if you don't do that, then there's no reason for you to live. He said, if you don't want to do what you were created for, bring him before me and end his existence.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
“And another came, saying, Lord, behold, here is thy pound, which I have kept laid up in a napkin.” See that? Hirelings. I kept it laid up; I didn't do anything with the knowledge you bestowed on me, the faith you gave me.

“Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.” Many will say they prophesied and did many wonderful works in his name, “And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.” That goes back to this servant: he was in the truth, and he took his talent and hid it in a napkin. I'm not helping them any more; I did it full time, but I don't want to do it any more.

And the end of the parable: “But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me.” Churches don't read that; they will look at it and say, no, we're not reading that in Sunday school. It means you are not just going to be able to do what you want to do. You were put on this earth to do what the Most High and Christ said, and if you don't do that, there's no reason for you to live. If you don't want to do what you were created for, bring him before me and end his existence.

precepts.text: Judge not, and ye shall not be judged: condemn not, and ye shall not be condemned. The judging Christ forbids is condemning someone. You cannot pronounce a person damned; judge not before the time, because you may be headed to the same place you are sending him.
precepts.point: And why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother's eye, but considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye? Thou hypocrite, first cast out the beam out of thine own eye; and then shalt thou see clearly to cast out the mote out of thy brother's eye.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

precepts.why:
“Judge not, that ye be not judged” is Christianity's favorite scripture, so go to Luke to see what it means: “Judge not, and ye shall not be judged: condemn not, and ye shall not be condemned.” Luke explains Matthew. To judge here means to condemn someone. Judge not, condemn not: that is the precept of it.

So you cannot say someone is damned. You cannot say someone blasphemed the Holy Ghost. That ain't your call to make and that ain't your place. Vengeance and judgment belong to the Lord. “Judge nothing before the time, until the Lord come”, who will bring to light the hidden things of darkness; in that day we will all know who made it and who didn't, and who was doing right or only pretending to.

And look at the one making the call. I'm going to say he blasphemed the Holy Ghost, but I'm out here messing with these hoes, endorsing gang culture, going to the bars and getting drunk every other week, robbing women and robbing my congregation and spending their hard-earned money on my clothes and debauchery. But he's condemned? Get out of here, man. Judge not before the time, because your behind might go to the same place their behind is going.

That is Matthew 7 read with Luke 6: “For with what judgment ye judge, ye shall be judged”; with what condemning you condemn, you'll be condemned too. You say your brother blasphemed while a beam is in your own eye and you are blaspheming more. Thou hypocrite, first cast out the beam out of thine own eye. We are all a work in progress, and the same mercy God had on David and Manasseh can be extended to you.

precepts.text: Whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock. These sayings are Christ's words: if you love me, keep my commandments. We have built this house, this congregation, on Christ, on the laws of God and faith in him.
precepts.point: On the 501c3 accusation: a 501c3 is just a tax classification, meaning we do not pay tax; when we spend at the store we keep the tax money and buy more unleavened bread. It is not a check that gets cut. And if you think we had to stop teaching the commandments and faith in Christ for it, look what we are teaching; nobody cut the feed and nobody cut the funding.

note.label: Member's In The Body

precepts.why:
“For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.” Christ tells us how to build on him: “Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock”.

These sayings of mine are Christ's words. What did Christ say? If you love me, keep my commandments. What else did he say? That anybody teaching against keeping the commandments is going to be least in the kingdom of heaven.

This is what we have done here. We have built this house, this congregation, this organization on Christ, on the laws of God and faith in him. We surrounded ourselves with those who decided to build on the proper foundation, and that is why this house stands.

precepts.text: Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, and then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity. There are going to be sisters that find out they are not going to get the kingdom because they did not respect nor reverence their husband. I taught classes, I handed out flyers, I did not eat pork; I never knew you. Sister, every command your husband gives you is law, as long as he is not asking you to sin; it is sin if you do not do it.
precepts.point: Sisters, if you only knew: a righteous man will do almost anything to see you happy. The teaching from the teacher's own daughter: she comes running to the door, keeps her demeanor sweet, and can get anything from him; she knows her role and plays it well. If you want, you have to be a princess. Reverence him, make him feel like he is everything he is supposed to be, and watch what happens. All sisters were taught to use the physical to get what they want; a righteous man needs your spirit to be right, and then you will see that Ephesians 5 man you desperately want.

note.label: Respect: The Evidence Of Her Faith

precepts.why:
“Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord.” The same respect you would show to Christ is the respect you should show your husband. There are going to be sisters who find out they are not going to get the kingdom because they did not respect nor reverence their husband. Some sisters said, damn, so we're going to go to hell because we're disrespectful? Yes. You didn't realize that?

“Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works?” They are going to have the audacity: Lord, I taught classes, I was out in the streets handing out flyers, I didn't eat pork, I left the shrimp alone, I wore fringes every day. “And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.”

What could keep them from knowing the Lord? Iniquity: sin. Sister, every command your husband gives you is law. It is like getting orders from God for you. As long as your husband is not asking you to sin, if he asks you to do something, it is sin if you don't do it.

In the westernized mindset that doesn't compute: he has that much power? You malfunction because you don't believe he is a god; you don't see the Christ in him. You had better read your Bible. He absolutely has that much authority over you, and all the wonderful works in the world will not cover the iniquity of disrespecting him.

precepts.text: Prophesying, casting out devils and doing wonderful works in the name, and still being told, I never knew you; depart from me, ye that work iniquity.
precepts.point: They prophesied in his name, cast out devils in his name, did many wonderful works and had the true name, and he still says, I never knew you; depart from me, ye that work iniquity. Working iniquity means breaking God's laws.

precepts.text: Not everyone that saith Lord shall enter, but he that doeth the will of the Father, lest the Lord say depart from me.
precepts.point: Yet Jehu takes no heed to walk in the law of the Most High with all his heart, showing that a man may do great things and still turn away and stay in sin.

note.label: 2 Kings 10: Jehu Destroys Baal and Falls Short of the Law

precepts.why:
“Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.” Many will say they prophesied, cast out devils and “done many wonderful works”, and the answer will be, “I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.”

Jehu did wonderful works in the Lord’s name. He destroyed Baal out of Israel. But he did not do the will of the Father with all his heart; he kept the golden calves. Great works do not stand in the place of walking in the law.

precepts.text: Do not give what is holy to the dogs nor cast your pearls before swine; the pearls are the word of the Most High, not to be handed to strangers.
precepts.point: Giving your honour to others is like giving what is holy to strangers. Too often our people care more about the other nations repenting and getting into the kingdom than about our own repentance, and want the other nations ruling with us in the kingdom.

note.label: Proverbs 5: The Strange Woman and Thy Labours in the House of a Stranger

precepts.why:
“Remove thy way far from her, and come not nigh the door of her house: Lest thou give thine honour unto others, and thy years unto the cruel”. Giving your honour to others is like giving what is holy to strangers.

Christ says: “Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet, and turn again and rend you.” The pearls are the word of the Most High, not to be handed to strangers. Hand it to the dogs and the swine and they trample it and turn and rend you.

Too often our people care more about the other nations repenting and getting into the kingdom than about our own repentance, and want the other nations ruling with us in the kingdom. That is giving your honour to others and your years to the cruel. Remove your way far from her.

precepts.text: Christ speaks of the strait gate and narrow way that leadeth unto life, which few find.
precepts.point: The gates are opened that the righteous nation which keepeth the truth may enter in, and that nation is the remnant that keeps the commandments. Whose mind is stayed on the Most High is kept in perfect peace because he trusteth in Him.

note.label: Isaiah 26: A Song of Salvation and the Straight Gate

precepts.why:
The gates opened for “the righteous nation which keepeth the truth” are the strait gate Christ speaks of: “Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat: Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.”

Few find it; that is why it is a remnant, the ones keeping the commandments, who enter the strong city in the land of Judah in that day.

precepts.text: Everyone that heareth His sayings and doeth them not is likened to a foolish man who built his house upon the sand, and great was the fall of it.
precepts.point: Even the great men who should have known the way have altogether broken the yoke and burst the bonds.

note.label: Jeremiah 5: None That Executeth Judgment

precepts.why:
“And every one that heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them not, shall be likened unto a foolish man, which built his house upon the sand”, and great was the fall of it. That is what foolish means here. The poor are foolish; they “know not the way of the Lord, nor the judgment of their God”, for when you sin you should know a judgment comes behind it. They hear and do not do, and their house is built on sand.

And it is not only the poor. Even the great men, who “have known the way of the Lord, and the judgment of their God”, who should have known the way, “have altogether broken the yoke, and burst the bonds.” Great was the fall of it.

precepts.text: Wide is the gate and broad the way that leadeth to destruction which many find, but strait is the gate and narrow the way which leadeth unto life, and few find it.
precepts.point: Ephraim being the firstborn means Israel is the firstborn of the Most High, set higher than the kings of the earth, who are the other nations, so all of Israel shall be over all the nations; the reason Ephraim was singled out is the tribes were not the first tribe that came, but the promise is to all Israel.

note.label: Jeremiah 31: The New Covenant

precepts.why:
Christ says the same thing about the way: “Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat”.

“Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.” Wide is the gate and broad the way to destruction, and many find it; the narrow way to life, few find. It is the one only path between the fire and the water in 2 Esdras 7, and the straight way of Jeremiah 31:9. Keeping God's laws is the narrow way, and that is the way he causes the remnant of Israel to walk in.

precepts.text: Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father.
precepts.point: Calling on his name while breaking the commandments is exactly this. Men bless what the law calls an abomination and still say Lord, Lord.

note.label: Matthew 25: The Ten Virgins, the Talents, and the Sheep and the Goats

precepts.why:
The foolish virgins came afterward saying, “Lord, Lord, open to us”, and were answered, “Verily I say unto you, I know you not.” Christ had already said who gets in: “Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.”

Saying Lord, Lord is not enough. The foolish took their lamps and took no oil with them, and the oil is the wisdom of the scriptures. Calling on his name while breaking the commandments is exactly this. Men bless what the law calls an abomination and still say Lord, Lord, and the door is shut on them.

The one who enters is the one who does the will of the Father. That is the difference between the wise and the foolish.

precepts.text: He taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes, because the spirit of the Most High was on him.
precepts.point: Peter was fearless and intrepid, a man who drew a sword and cut off the man's ear, which was not the first time he used it; he came from the streets, and we have brothers with that same posture. They took knowledge the disciples had been with Christ because you take on the attributes and characteristics of whoever you surround yourself with, and the disciples all spoke the same thing as Christ.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

precepts.why:
“For he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.” The spirit of the Most High was on Christ, and it came through in how he taught.

Brothers who teach weak, like the Christian pastors, with no power and no conviction, are lacking the Holy Spirit. The boldness of Peter and John was the same authority that was on Christ. People who call us hostile have simply never seen a man of God speak with the Holy Spirit.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 14 Part 2

precepts.why:
Some of the two thirds come through these doors and are sitting in the seats right now. “Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven”: they say Lord, Lord because they may be in camps, they know they are Israel. All you Israelites ain’t getting into the kingdom of heaven. “But he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven”: he that follows the Lamb whithersoever he goes.

“Have we not prophesied in thy name?” We used to be in the streets teaching that Israelite stuff, we did videos for you, Lord. “And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.” There comes a burnout: your spirit loses interest in the word of God, you get tired of discipline day after day, you lean toward adultery, toward sin, you join with the brother you know is the devil, the beard comes off. Know your spirit.

note.label: A Tree Bearing No Fruits

points: Every good tree bringeth forth good fruit, but a corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit; a brother who keeps doing evil and does not repent is a corrupt tree. Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down and cast into the fire, which is damnation. Examine yourself, and understand why the deacon keeps his distance from some who bring forth evil fruit unrepented. Not every one that saith Lord, Lord shall enter the kingdom.

note.label: I Need More Confidence

points: For he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes. So Christ taught with authority. He taught with power. He did not teach like the scribes taught. He was not teaching it like the people in the Christian church teach, all the hooping and hollering. He was not teaching soft. Christ was a man's man. He was aggressive. The Bible says he was an austere man. Christ was bold. Christ was full of confidence. So if we claim to be disciples of Christ, if we claim to follow Christ, if we claim to have the spirit of Christ, we have got to roll how Christ rolled.
